question_text:
This table shows the distribution of marks obtained on a logic test.

| Mark | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frequency | 1 | 3 | 5 | 8 | 4 | 2 | 0 | 1 |

Use technology to find the mean and population standard deviation of the test scores.

subparts.stem: Use technology to find the mean and population standard deviation of the test scores.

mark_breakdown.desc: Entering frequency table data into calculator or calculating $\sum f = 24$, $\sum fx = 142$

subparts.solution:
Using technology for the frequency distribution:
$$\sum f = n = 24$$
$$\sum fx = 142$$
$$\bar{x} = \frac{142}{24} = 5.9166... \approx 5.92$$
$$\sigma \approx 1.4976... \approx 1.50$$
The mean test score is $\mu \approx 5.92$, and the population standard deviation is $\sigma \approx 1.50$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For a discrete frequency distribution, $\mu = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ and $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f} - \mu^2}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Not including frequencies when calculating the mean and standard deviation (i.e. averaging the distinct mark values).
